A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same C-MCTD research and contain 24 readable pages, including Appendices A–C. Text comparison and page rendering establish that the scientific text, equations, figures, tables, and algorithms match.

before.justification: v1 reports original C-MCTD experiments on maze navigation, cube manipulation, and visual navigation in Section 5, with additional ablations and runtime analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix B, including success rates, planning times, and component ablations.

M1.justification: The Online, Distributed, and Preplan Composer methods are identical, including guidance sets, fast replanning, graph construction, and manipulation plan caching. The detailed algorithms in Appendix C also match.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same PointMaze and AntMaze scales, single- through quadruple-cube manipulation tasks, and medium/large visual mazes. Training datasets and additional test scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within every corresponding experiment, including the Diffuser, Diffusion Forcing, and MCTD variants, plus SSD and CompDiffuser where evaluated. CompDiffuser remains excluded from the runtime comparison in Table 13.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A retain identical preprocessing, model configurations, controllers, planning horizons, search budgets, and evaluation metrics. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Appendix B retains the same guidance-set, fast-replanning, stitching-threshold, and plan-cache ablations, together with graph-construction overhead analysis. The qualitative planning comparison in Figure 4 is also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both specify 50 runs comprising 5 tasks × 10 seeds and use the same mean and standard-deviation reporting. Run-count disclosures and uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results in Tables 1–4 and 9–13, accompanying findings, and qualitative examples match. For example, Preplan Composer achieves 100 ± 0% success on PointMaze-Giant in Table 1 in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), trajectory definitions, distribution factorizations, and graph-connection formulations are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: compositional inference-time planning through three Composer variants, improved long-horizon performance, and planning up to 10 times beyond training lengths without model retraining.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations remain identical, including computational tradeoffs, waypoint difficulties in visual tasks, task-dependent suitability, limited generalization to novel environments, and challenges with stochastic dynamics.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains identical hardware, training-time disclosures, hyperparameter tables, data-processing instructions, and implementation information. Code-access references also match; the added funding acknowledgment supplies no new reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 4, research-positioning statements, and all 34 cited works are unchanged. The acknowledgment addition introduces no citation or change in the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 adds the GRDC Cooperative Hub Program grant RS-2024-00436165 to the funding acknowledgment and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose, terminology, and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded acknowledgment slightly reflows the References section on page 11, and the margin stamp changes on page 1. Figures, tables, algorithm displays, and all other page renderings are identical.

improvement.justification: v2 provides more complete funding attribution on page 11, with minor accompanying layout and version-stamp changes. The scientific content and all appendices are unchanged, leaving the paper's rigor, evidential support, reproducibility, and overall clarity materially equivalent.
